title: Protocol
description: One health or performance protocol: a concrete behavior with its rationale, evidence grade, citations, and the observable signals that indicate trying it.

id.description: Stable snake_case identifier. Must equal the filename without .json. Never reuse or rename a published id.

name.description: Short Title-Case noun phrase, 2-5 words, naming the behavior plainly. No person names, no metaphors. Example: "Post-Meal Walk".

title.description: One plain imperative sentence saying what to do, ending in a period. No semicolons, colons, or questions. Example: "Walk after one meal per day."

benefit.description: One short plain outcome phrase, saying what the person gets: energy, focus, output, sleep, or recovery. 14 words or fewer. Do not address the reader directly. Example: "Steadier energy after lunch."

subtitle.description: Two or three word Title Case category label, no punctuation. Example: "Meal Protocol".

rationale.description: One or two plain sentences explaining why the protocol works. No person names as the subject (attribution belongs in `origin`), no semicolons or colons.

origin.description: Optional attribution: one plain sentence naming who is known for the practice and what they did. Example: "Jeff Bezos replaced slides with six-page narrative memos at Amazon."

family.description: Optional progression ladder this protocol belongs to. Every family must contain exactly one beginner, one intermediate, and one advanced protocol.

tier.description: Rung on the family ladder. Required when family is set, forbidden otherwise.

tierTarget.description: The measurable bar that counts as holding this rung, e.g. "60 screen-free minutes before sleep". Required when family is set.

targets.description: Outcome labels the protocol aims at, e.g. "Sleep", "Focus", "VO2 max".

durationMinutes.description: Typical minutes one session or setup of this protocol takes.

grade.description: strong: consistent trial, meta-analytic, or guideline-level support. moderate: supportive trials or robust observational evidence with limitations. emerging: early, small, or mixed evidence. anecdotal: practice-driven with a plausible mechanism but little direct trial evidence.

summary.description: One sentence stating what the evidence shows, written no stronger than the grade supports.

sources.description: Citations backing the summary: studies, meta-analyses, position stands, or guidelines.

indications.description: Observable signals that suggest trying this protocol, each a complete sentence ending in a period, phrased neutrally so an agent can match them against a person's data. Example: "Wake time swings by hours between weekdays and weekends."

avoidWhen.description: Contraindications and situations where the protocol should not be attempted.

guide.description: One canonical external how-to page for first-timers, or an explicit null after checking that no external page earns the slot. Distinct from evidence sources.
